data.message: Retrieving the official financial statement PDF from the CSE document repository
Document secured and staged for processing
Running multi-dimensional financial health diagnostics with LLM (this may take a minute)...
Health diagnostics finalised for COMB.N0000 — overall score: 88/100 · Good

standardHealthChecks.name: Liquidity Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Liquidity metrics are exceptionally strong and well above statutory minimums, with Rupee LCR at 368.83% and All Currency LCR at 282.77% (against the 100% statutory requirement), complemented by a Net Stable Funding Ratio of 165.35%.

standardHealthChecks.name: Profitability Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Group profit for the period grew by 19.80% YoY to Rs. 17.94 billion. Profitability ratios improved, with Return on Equity reaching 21.37% (up from 19.51% at end-2025) and Return on Assets (before tax) rising to 3.21%.

standardHealthChecks.name: Debt Management
standardHealthChecks.description: Maintains a conservative debt profile with a Debt-to-Equity ratio of 22.38% and strong interest coverage of 14.40x. Capital buffers easily absorb existing subordinated liabilities.

standardHealthChecks.name: Cash Flow Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Generated robust net cash flows from operating activities of Rs. 13.35 billion for the quarter, leaving total cash and cash equivalents at a solid Rs. 98.70 billion.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR)
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Tier 1 Capital Ratio stood at 13.32% (Bank) / 13.09% (Group) against the regulatory minimum of 10.00%, while Total Capital Ratio reached 16.85% (Bank) / 16.50% (Group) against the 14.00% minimum requirement.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Capital Adequacy measures a bank's financial strength and capacity to absorb operational and credit losses while complying with Basel III regulations.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Asset Quality & Provision Coverage
dynamicHealthChecks.description: The Stage 3 impaired loans ratio improved significantly to 1.34% (down from 1.54% at end-2025), while provision coverage (Stage 3 impairment to Stage 3 loans) strengthened to 75.04%. Impairment charges dropped by 55.49% YoY.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Asset quality indicates the health of the bank's loan portfolio, directly affecting loan loss provisions and future capital preservation.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Net Interest Margin (NIM) & Deposit Mix
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Net Interest Margin remained healthy at 4.50%, supported by an industry-best CASA ratio of 40.18%, driving Net Interest Income up 13.44% YoY to Rs. 38.81 billion.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: NIM and CASA ratios reflect the bank's cost of funds and fundamental profitability from core intermediation activities.

recommendations: Leverage the industry-leading CASA ratio (40.18%) to maintain low cost-of-funds and protect Net Interest Margins in a shifting interest rate environment.
Monitor Stage 2 loan exposures closely as the overall loan book grows rapidly (+31.35% YoY) to prevent credit quality deterioration.
Manage operating expense growth (which rose 15.81% YoY) to preserve the lean cost-to-income ratio (currently 29.03% excluding financial service taxes).
Further expand fee-and-commission income and trade services to diversify non-interest revenue streams.
result.analysisNotes: Commercial Bank of Ceylon PLC delivered outstanding milestone financial results in Q1 2026, becoming Sri Lanka's first private sector banking group to exceed Rs. 3.5 trillion in assets (reaching Rs. 3.61 Tn, up 6.81% YTD). Bottom-line profit increased 19.80% YoY to Rs. 17.94 billion, supported by strong loan growth (+Rs. 71.6 Bn in Q1) and reduced impairment charges (-55.5% YoY). Asset quality and regulatory liquidity indicators remain extremely sound.
